opener: A prefab labour camp is the relocatable build in the SAMAN worker housing family: bolted light-steel panels on pedestal footings, with repeatable door and window modules and plug-and-play electrical blocks, so the same camp dismantles and re-erects at the next project. Blocks arrange around a central services spine to the approved site plan. Sizes span 60x24 ft G+1 through 120x24 ft G+2 for 58 to 216 workers a building, each priced ex-factory on the camp's own square-foot rate with a fixed quote in 48 hours.
descriptionHtml:
The Prefab Labour Camp: Housing That Moves With the Work

Most worker housing is written off when the project ends. The prefab labour camp is engineered so it is not. Wall, floor and roof panels share one bolted module, the block stands on pedestal pads instead of a poured slab, and electrical blocks plug together through external cable trays. When the project finishes, the camp unbolts, travels on trailers with panels numbered for reassembly, and stands again at the next site far faster than it first went up.

The Arithmetic of Moving

Rate for rate a camp runs a little above a fixed open-hall shed of the same size, and repays the difference the first time it moves. Across three projects the same block becomes the cheapest housing a contractor owns. Owners who repeat the block report a second erection needs about half the first one's hours, and pedestal footings mean leaving a site means lifting pads, never breaking concrete.

Every size is fully demountable, including both G+2 entries, whose third floor bolts onto the identical module the ground floor uses.

Engineering for Repeat Moves

Bolted light steel frames on pedestals form the skeleton; PUF or approved EPS panels in 50, 60 and 80 mm form the envelope; and repeatable door and window modules mean one damaged panel is exchanged instead of condemning the wall. Service entries are protected for transit, and the document set includes the block's move log. The Specifications tab lists every row of the build standard.

Camp Layouts

The blocks group along a single services spine carrying ring-main water and zoned power, hookup drawings issued per site. The wide-body size keeps a full utility zone indoors, which cold-region postings appreciate. Repeat customers carry one block numbering from site to site so the layout plan follows the buildings.

Camp Pricing

Rs 679.50 per square foot ex-GST at every size. Trailer counts and crane hours for a future move are stated on the quotation itself, so relocation is budgeted before purchase, not discovered after. Freight and fit-out are quoted separately, fixed within 48 hours.

Delivery, Erection, Re-erection

First delivery runs 7 to 21 working days from drawing approval. Erection is bolt-up on pre-marked pad positions from the ground template. Dismantling runs assembly in reverse, each numbered panel returning to its trailer. Warranty rides along: structure covered 5 years, finishing covered 1.

Why Buy the Camp From SAMAN

Because demountability is a factory discipline, not a site improvisation. Panel tolerances, module repeats and connection details are controlled where they are made. Crews wanting lockable rooms in a movable block should compare the room-block hutment first, and the full colony line-up shows the fixed buildings that cost less for the same area when nothing ever moves.

Prefab Labour Camp FAQs

How many times can the camp move?

The module is designed for repeated cycles; blocks in service have moved several times with panel swaps as the only maintenance.

How long does a move take?

Dismantling, transport and re-erection are quoted per site; the second build typically halves the first build's hours.

Does moving void the warranty?

Relocation by the documented procedure keeps warranty terms; the move log records each cycle.

Can it become permanent?

Yes, grouting the pedestals turns the block permanent, nothing altered structurally above the base line.

What foundations does it need?

Pedestal pads on compacted ground, positions pre-marked from the ground template supplied with the block.
